definition: A corner is the cut, where two card edges meet. It is not the printed frame. Rounding is the arc past the measured 10–90% edge rise. The radius comes from the tip setback and from a circle fit to the silhouette. They must agree within 0.1 mm, and the upright and 180° scans must agree within 0.1 mm. A setback inside either edge rise is withheld. Radius 0 is not published. Whitening is paper showing against the same border at mid-edge. A border that is already paper-white, or a pale patch that is foil glare, is withheld. A ding is a local notch in the cut. It is withheld when only one orientation shows it. Fraying is card-colored fiber outside the fitted cut. It is withheld when it does not rotate with the card. Length 0 is published only when both orientations are clean. A side the centering key has withheld does not grow a corner grade. TD-12 is excluded. TD-14 through TD-18, the flatbed backs, and the BGS labels are pending and are not measured here. Unapproved until the owner checks the overlay. No 0–10 corner score is assigned.

pendingScans.bgsLabels: Owner will write company, overall, centering, corners, edges, surface, and cert for his BGS slabs. No label is stored here.

phone: A phone corner is not scored. It waits until those two edges already match the centering key, on a still in the ±0.1 mm tier (at or above 30 px/mm) or the ±0.2 mm tier (from 15 px/mm up to 30).
